text:
Maria: quick update - ran the 72h sanity-probe across the new driver+fw combo on the canary rack (rack-7). results attached below, but high level: Xid events dropped significantly on 8/12 cards, ECC counters stable on most nodes.
Devin: nice, can you paste the key metrics?
Maria: summary: pre-patch Xid rate ~0.45/hr/card, post-patch ~0.12/hr/card on canary; average p95 latency unchanged. ECC correctables per day went from ~140 -> ~18 on affected nodes.
Kai: that's promising. where was the canary deployed? region wise?
Maria: us-west-2 only, mixed A100 v4 and A10G. we targeted nodes with historically high Xid churn.
AJ: what was the exact firmware + driver combo? we need to know compatibility delta.
Maria: driver 525.105.17 + fw 2.1.9 with kernel module built on 6.1.35. note: we used the runtime kernel-compat shim for one node (rack-7-node-4) to exercise fallback.
Devin: any odd crashes or panic logs?
Maria: one node had a kernel oops related to nvlink during stress-run, but it didn't produce a persistent Xid spike. logs: ```kernel: nvidia: timeout waiting for ... nvlink link retrain```
Kai: did we correlate with power/cooling telemetry? sometimes nvlink retrains track with temp spikes.
Maria: checked — temps stable, no fan anomalies. power draw slightly higher on one host but within range.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary-deploy completed by Maria at 1855007700, monitoring window started.
AJ: what's our plan to widen rollout? lean on burn-in or more telemetry sampling?
Devin: propose two steps: (1) extend canary to 50% of racks in us-west-2 with same HW mix for 48h; (2) enable verbose nv driver coredump sampling on a subset for another 48h. both gated behind a rollback job.
Maria: agreed. I also want to enable prefix/KV cache offload to make sure batching behavior didn't mask Xids. can we toggle that safely?
Kai: yes, we can flip cache off on a per-pool level. I'll schedule it during low traffic window.
AJ: add a synthetic workload that reproduces our highest token throughput path — that increases chance of hitting the failure mode.
Maria: added a runbook snippet and the synthetic runner config in the shared gist: https://short.url/sanity-probe-config
Devin: what thresholds should we use for auto-rollback? previous cutoff was 0.3/hr/card. keep that?
Maria: let's be stricter: rollback if Xid > 0.2/hr/card for >2 hosts over 1h, or ECC correctables increase >200% from baseline.
Kai: will add an alert in PagerDuty with that rule and a slack webhook to this thread.
ops-bot: alert-rule created: infra.gpu.sanity.xid_spike.canary by Kai at 1855012000.
AJ: any cost implications for extending canary? more burn-in = GPU hours.
Devin: minimal — we'll reuse idle capacity and schedule during low-cost windows; estimate +120 GPU-hours for the widened sweep.
Maria: next steps: (1) widen canary to 50% racks in us-west-2 (Kai) (2) enable nv verbose coredumps on subset (Devin) (3) run synthetic throughput test (AJ) (4) monitor for 48h, rollback on thresholds (Maria). I'll post a short summary after 24h.
Kai: ack, scheduling widen for 02:00 UTC tomorrow.
AJ: I'll prepare the synthetic job and share command.
Devin: I'll flip verbose coredumps and watch space usage; keep the sample window small to avoid disk fill.
Maria: 24h update: initial 24h looks good — canary Xid rate down ~70% vs pre-patch baseline, no new kernel oops beyond the one nvlink event. continuing to 48h then widen region if stable. thanks all :thumbsup:
